ABC News is in big trouble, again, for lying about the Trump family and then quietly deleting the report. Hopefully ABC News gets sued into bankruptcy over this. They falsely published a story on Wednesday that said Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump’s investment firm, 1789 Capital, had taken a major stake in a defense company called Anduril and that Anduril had then won more than $6 billion in Pentagon contracts. California Governor Gavin Newsom shared the story. The numbers were wrong, and Palmer Luckey says Anduril gave ABC News the correct figures before the story went up.

This is what the fake news media does. They publish lies, do the damage by getting those lies amplified, and then quietly retract the stories. This is an unforgivable pattern of malicious behavior and ABC News needs to pay the price. Make a legal example out of them.

Here’s the true story. Anduril is a private defense technology company founded by Palmer Luckey, the entrepreneur who created the Oculus virtual-reality headset. Anduril builds autonomous drones and other military systems. 1789 Capital is a venture-capital firm where Donald Trump Jr. is one of six partners. ABC News reported that 1789 Capital had taken a major stake in Anduril out of a $2.5 billion funding round. Luckey says 1789 Capital actually invested $50 million, which is roughly one one-thousandth of his Anduril company valued at more than $60 billion. He also says most of the $6 billion figure was a contract ceiling with the government, the maximum the government is allowed to spend, not money it has actually committed to Anduril. These facts are of enormous significance and if truthfully reported would’ve taken all punch out of the ABC News piece.

The editors at ABC News reviewed the piece, made a small edit, and stood by it. Then ABC News deleted the page. No note. No explanation. And certainly no apology. The link went dead. Brian Stelter says a source told him the story was “published prematurely.” Luckey says that’s a cover. The author has gone quiet. ABC News has since put up a corrected version with an editor’s note admitting errors on the investments, contracts, and timeline. My guess is they’re still talking to their legal department about lawsuits from the Trump sons.

A news organization does not get to put false numbers into the world, watch Democrats spread them, and then erase the article when the target answers with the ledger. Correct it on the same page or don’t publish it. Better yet, just publish the truth. As I’ve said before, it’s much more powerful.

I hope Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump sue ABC News for billions. That’s the only way these propagandist media companies will ever stop, when they go bankrupt.
